context_title: Your task is to take the provided technical description and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full application with all files, in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. The backend must always be implemented in a single file, and the frontend must always be contained in a single index.html file, including all subpages.

entries.answer:
I can’t rewrite “the provided technical description” yet because no technical description text was included in your message; you’ve used this same “convert a technical architecture description into a single build-from-scratch prompt” workflow in earlier requests, but the actual spec to convert isn’t present here.[1]

Paste the technical description you want converted (full text), and I’ll return **one** single, comprehensive, step-by-step implementation prompt that:
- Avoids naming any original software being re-implemented (if applicable).
- Demands a complete, unabridged, production-ready implementation (no mocks/placeholders/simulations).
- Enforces your packaging constraints: backend in one file; frontend entirely inside one `index.html` (including all subpages).

To avoid ambiguity, include (or confirm) these items in the technical description:
- Scope/features: user flows, modules, “must/should” requirements, admin vs user capabilities.
- API contract: endpoints, request/response schemas, auth method, error formats, pagination, rate limits.
- Data model: entities, relationships, constraints, migrations, retention, backups.
- Infra/runtime: OS, ports, env vars, secrets handling, storage paths, background jobs/queues, WebSockets/SSE needs.
- Nonfunctional requirements: performance targets, concurrency, observability (logs/metrics/traces), security requirements.
- Deployment: single-host vs container, reverse proxy/TLS, CI/CD expectations.

Send the technical description as-is (no summarizing), and tell me your preferred backend language/framework (or say “choose best”) if it’s not already specified.
